description: Figure 6 (left plot) illustrates how the number of datasets changes over time by researcher location, showing separate colored bars for the five most frequent locations plus an “Other” category. The horizontal axis is labeled “Year” and lists years from 2012 through 2022 in chronological order. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at approximately \(10^0\), \(10^1\), and \(10^2\). The legend titled “Researcher Location” maps colors to categories: Other (blue), USA (orange), IN (green), UK (red), IT (purple), and DE (brown). For each year, multiple narrow vertical bars appear side-by-side (grouped by year), one per location category when present; early years (2012–2015) show only small bars near \(10^0\)–a few units, while later years include taller bars reaching into the tens and up to around \(10^2\). The “Other” (blue) bars are present across many years and become the tallest in the later period, reaching roughly \(10^2\) around 2021, while the USA (orange) bars also rise into the tens (roughly \(10^1\) to several \(10^1\)) in later years; UK (red), IT (purple), DE (brown), and IN (green) appear intermittently with heights generally in the single digits to tens depending on year. No bars are visually emphasized beyond the color coding, and the categories are not sorted by bar height; they are distinguished by the legend and repeated consistently across the grouped yearly clusters.
